question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a new authorization boundary and config grammar that can change operator security posture across message, gateway, sender, sandbox, and plugin paths.

options.title: Design generic action policy
options.body: Add a typed, documented action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with explicit precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.

options.title: Narrow to message and gateway
options.body: Add separate message and gateway action controls only, reducing immediate scope but risking parallel policy surfaces and future drift.

options.title: Defer to confirmation work
options.body: Leave static action deny out of core for now and rely on the related confirmation-gate design, accepting that deny-style least privilege remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Design generic action policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed, documented action-aware policy grammar enforced before multiplexed tool actions execute, with explicit precedence and trusted-context tests for message and gateway.
